gloss: Pointing at a deer and calling it a horse; to distort facts.
teaser: Ever heard of calling a deer a horse? Let’s explore the meaning behind this intriguing phrase.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever heard of calling a deer a horse? Let’s explore the meaning behind this intriguing phrase.[break 1s] The phrase is: 指鹿为马, zhǐ lù wéi mǎ.[break 0.5s] 指 (zhǐ) means 'to point';[break 0.5s] 鹿 (lù) means 'deer';[break 0.5s] 为 (wéi) means 'to be';[break 0.5s] 马 (mǎ) means 'horse'.[break 1s] So, the full idiom 指鹿为马 literally means 'to point at a deer and call it a horse' and figuratively means 'to distort facts or lie'.[break 1s] Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s] This idiom originates from a historical event during the Qin Dynasty. A powerful official named Zhao Gao once pointed at a deer and insisted it was a horse to test the loyalty of his courtiers. Those who went along with his claim were seen as loyal, while those who disagreed faced dire consequences. This act symbolized the manipulation of truth for personal gain.[break 1.5s] Example 1: 他说的都是谎言，正是指鹿为马。  He is just telling lies, it’s truly pointing at a deer and calling it a horse.[break 1s] Example 2: 在这个公司里，有些人喜欢指鹿为马。  In this company, some people enjoy distorting the truth.[break 1s] Example 3: 我们不能容忍指鹿为马的行为。  We cannot tolerate the act of distorting the facts.[break 1s] So, once again, 指鹿为马 means to distort facts. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
